claim: Preeclampsia is a severe complication of late pregnancy and is the second leading cause of maternal mortality in the US, affecting 8% of first-time pregnancies.
source: Preeclampsia (PE) is a severe complication of late pregnancy and is the second leading cause of maternal mortality in the US, affecting 8% of first-time pregnancies (Gifford, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gifford, 2000

claim: PE is characterized by the onset of hypertension, proteinuria, and other signs of maternal vascular damage that contributes to maternal and neonatal mortality and morbidity.
source: PE is characterized by the onset of hypertension, proteinuria, and other signs of maternal vascular damage that contributes to maternal and neonatal mortality and morbidity (Gifford, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gifford, 2000

claim: Severe preeclampsia is diagnosed based on elevated blood pressure (systolic ≥160 or diastolic of ≥100 mm Hg) or thrombocytopenia, impaired liver function, progressive renal insufficiency, pulmonary edema, or the onset of cerebral or visual disturbances.
source: Severe preeclampsia (sPE) is diagnosed based on elevated blood pressure (systolic ≥160 or diastolic of ≥100 mm Hg) or thrombocytopenia, impaired liver function, progressive renal insufficiency, pulmonary edema, or the onset of cerebral or visual disturbances (Gynecologists ACoOa, Pregnancy TFoHi, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to clinical guidelines

claim: sPE is a placental insufficiency syndrome mediated by early-deficient extravillous trophoblast invasion of uterine decidua and spiral arterioles, leading to incomplete endovascular invasion and altered uteroplacental perfusion.
source: sPE is a placental insufficiency syndrome mediated by early-deficient extravillous trophoblast (EVT) invasion of uterine decidua and spiral arterioles, leading to incomplete endovascular invasion and altered uteroplacental perfusion (Roberts and Cooper, 2001; Brosens et al., 2019; Staff et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Pregnancy health is dictated by the embryo, placenta, and the quality of the maternal decidua, where EVTs invasion and remodeling of maternal spiral arteries occur.
source: Pregnancy health is dictated by the embryo, placenta, and the quality of the maternal decidua, where EVTs invasion and remodeling of maternal spiral arteries occur (Norwitz et al., 2001; Cha et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Norwitz et al., 2001 and Cha et al., 2012

claim: Accumulated evidence suggests that the contribution of the decidua to the etiology of PE, sPE, and placenta accreta is significant.
source: Accumulated evidence suggests that the contribution of the decidua to the etiology of PE (Rabaglino et al., 2015), sPE (Garrido-Gomez et al., 2017; Garrido-Gomez et al., 2020; Garrido-Gómez et al., 2020), and placenta accreta (McNally et al., 2020) is significant, and cellular signaling in the decidua may determine whether these conditions develop.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Decidualization is the remodeling of the endometrium initiated after ovulation that is necessary for adequate trophoblast invasion and subsequent placentation.
source: Decidualization is the remodeling of the endometrium initiated after ovulation that is necessary for adequate trophoblast invasion and subsequent placentation (Gellersen and Brosens, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gellersen and Brosens, 2014

claim: Defective decidualization entails the inability of the endometrial compartment to undertake tissue differentiation, leading to aberrations in placentation and compromising pregnancy health.
source: Defective decidualization (DD) entails the inability of the endometrial compartment to undertake tissue differentiation, leading to aberrations in placentation and compromising pregnancy health (Garrido-Gómez et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Garrido-Gómez et al., 2020

claim: In humans and other great apes, the formation of the decidua is a conceptus-independent process driven by progesterone and the second messenger cyclic adenosine monophosphate.
source: In humans and other great apes, the formation of the decidua is a conceptus-independent process driven by progesterone and the second messenger cyclic adenosine monophosphate (Brar et al., 1997) that stimulates synthesis of a complex network of intracellular and secreted proteins through progesterone receptor (PR) activation.
evidence: Supported by citation to Brar et al., 1997

claim: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands.
source: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands (Kelleher et al., 2018), influx of specialized immune cells, vascular remodeling, and morphological (Dunn et al., 2003; Ramathal et al., 2010), biochemical (Giudice et al., 1998; Jabbour and Critchley, 2001), and transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kelleher et al., 2018

claim: Endometrial decidualization involves influx of specialized immune cells.
source: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands (Kelleher et al., 2018), influx of specialized immune cells, vascular remodeling, and morphological (Dunn et al., 2003; Ramathal et al., 2010), biochemical (Giudice et al., 1998; Jabbour and Critchley, 2001), and transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated as part of decidualization process description

claim: Endometrial decidualization involves vascular remodeling.
source: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands (Kelleher et al., 2018), influx of specialized immune cells, vascular remodeling, and morphological (Dunn et al., 2003; Ramathal et al., 2010), biochemical (Giudice et al., 1998; Jabbour and Critchley, 2001), and transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated as part of decidualization process description

claim: Endometrial decidualization involves morphological reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment.
source: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands (Kelleher et al., 2018), influx of specialized immune cells, vascular remodeling, and morphological (Dunn et al., 2003; Ramathal et al., 2010), biochemical (Giudice et al., 1998; Jabbour and Critchley, 2001), and transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dunn et al., 2003 and Ramathal et al., 2010

claim: Endometrial decidualization involves biochemical reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment.
source: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands (Kelleher et al., 2018), influx of specialized immune cells, vascular remodeling, and morphological (Dunn et al., 2003; Ramathal et al., 2010), biochemical (Giudice et al., 1998; Jabbour and Critchley, 2001), and transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Giudice et al., 1998 and Jabbour and Critchley, 2001

claim: Endometrial decidualization involves transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment.
source: Endometrial decidualization involves secretory transformation of uterine glands (Kelleher et al., 2018), influx of specialized immune cells, vascular remodeling, and morphological (Dunn et al., 2003; Ramathal et al., 2010), biochemical (Giudice et al., 1998; Jabbour and Critchley, 2001), and transcriptional reprogramming of the endometrial stromal compartment (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2020

claim: The transcriptomics of human decidualization at single-cell resolution from secretory endometrial samples showed that the process is initiated gradually after ovulation, with a direct interplay between stromal fibroblasts and lymphocytes.
source: We recently characterized the transcriptomics of human decidualization at single-cell resolution from secretory endometrial samples and showed that the process is initiated gradually after ovulation, with a direct interplay between stromal fibroblasts and lymphocytes (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2020

claim: A total of 40 non-pregnant women who experienced a previous pregnancy were enrolled in this study for endometrial RNA-sequencing analysis.
source: A total of 40 non-pregnant women who experienced a previous pregnancy were enrolled in this study for endometrial RNA-sequencing analysis.
evidence: Directly stated in study design section

claim: Endometrial samples were obtained during late secretory phase in 24 women who had developed sPE in a previous pregnancy and in 16 women with no history of sPE.
source: Endometrial samples were obtained for research purposes during late secretory phase in 24 women who had developed sPE in a previous pregnancy and in 16 women with no history of sPE with full term (n = 8) and preterm pregnancies (n = 8) as controls.
evidence: Directly stated in study design section

claim: The experimental design was based on a stratified random sampling with a 70:30 proportion in two cohorts: a training (n = 29) and validation (n = 11) set of samples.
source: The experimental design was based on a stratified random sampling with a 70:30 proportion in two cohorts: a training (n = 29) and validation (n = 11) set of samples.
evidence: Directly stated in study design section

claim: The training set of samples was analyzed by RNA-seq to identify the global transcriptomic profiling changes between control (n = 12) and sPE (n = 17) samples.
source: The training set of samples was analyzed by RNA-seq to identify the global transcriptomic profiling changes between control (n = 12) and sPE (n = 17) samples.
evidence: Directly stated in study design section

claim: Transcriptional analysis in the training set revealed 593 DEGs based on FDR < 0.05 and with at least 1.2 FC between groups.
source: This comparison revealed 593 DEGs based on FDR < 0.05 and with at least 1.2 FC between groups (FC ≥ 1.2).
evidence: Directly stated result from RNA-seq analysis

claim: A total of 155 upregulated and 438 downregulated DEGs were identified as being associated with DD in sPE.
source: A total of 155 upregulated and 438 downregulated DEGs were identified as being associated with DD in sPE (Figure 1C; complete list in Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Directly stated result from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Downregulated transcripts include those involved in decidualization, such as MMP3, PRL, IL-6, and IHH.
source: Downregulated transcripts include those involved in decidualization, such as MMP3, PRL, IL-6, and IHH; and genes associated with signaling (e.g., NR4A3 and IL8), growth factors (e.g., FGF1 and FGF7), angiogenesis (e.g., EDN2 and TMEM215), and immune response (CCL20, CXCL3, and IGHG1).
evidence: Directly stated result from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Upregulated genes are involved in amino acid metabolic/catabolic processes (IDO2 and CAPN3), transport, and oxidoreductase activity.
source: Upregulated genes are involved in amino acid metabolic/catabolic processes (IDO2 and CAPN3), transport, and oxidoreductase activity.
evidence: Directly stated result from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Nine genes were overlapped between in vitro DD (n = 129) and in vivo DD (n = 593) datasets in sPE compared to control women.
source: Here, we compared DD overlapping between DEGs reported in vitro (n = 129) vs. in vivo (n = 593) in sPE compared to control women. Nine genes were overlapped between the two datasets (Figure 2A); one gene was upregulated (ERP27), and eight genes were downregulated (e.g., ISM1, MEST, MFAP2, and REEP2).
evidence: Directly stated comparison result

claim: 263 genes from the 593 DEGs in sPE vs. control are expressed by hESC.
source: We found that 263 genes from the 593 DEGs in sPE vs. control are expressed by hESC (Figure 2C).
evidence: Directly stated result from comparison with single-cell data

claim: A transcriptomic signature encoding DD detected in sPE in vivo comprises 120 genes with significant dysregulation (FDR < 0.05) and at least 1.4-fold increase (FC ≥1.4) between sPE and control with assigned EntrezID.
source: To formulate the transcriptomic signature that encodes DD detected in sPE in vivo, we selected genes with significant dysregulation (FDR < 0.05) and at least 1.4-fold increase (FC ≥1.4) between sPE and control with assigned EntrezID. A volcano plot shows 120 DEGs meeting these criteria included in the final DD signature (Figure 3A; complete list of genes is included in Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Directly stated result from gene selection criteria

claim: GO analysis of the gene signature associated with DD in sPE identified 151 enriched biological processes downregulated (FDR < 0.05).
source: GO analysis of the gene signature associated with DD in sPE identified 151 enriched biological processes downregulated (FDR < 0.05).
evidence: Directly stated result from GO analysis

claim: The enriched biological processes were associated with cell cycle, DNA damage response, cell signaling, cellular response, cell motility, extracellular matrix, immune response, and reproductive process.
source: These pathways were associated with cell cycle, DNA damage response, cell signaling, cellular response, cell motility, extracellular matrix, immune response, and reproductive process (Figure 3B).
evidence: Directly stated result from GO analysis

claim: Based on the 120 genes included in the DD signature, PCA showed that sPE and control samples clustered separately in two groups, except for three control samples (C20, C21, and C22).
source: Based on the 120 genes included in the DD signature, PCA showed that sPE and control samples clustered separately in two groups, except for three control samples (C20, C21, and C22) (Figure 4A).
evidence: Directly stated result from PCA analysis with reference to Figure 4A

claim: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis confirmed that gene fingerprinting effectively segregated the two groups: one encompassing mainly controls and the other mainly sPE samples.
source: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis confirmed that gene fingerprinting effectively segregated the two groups: one encompassing mainly controls and the other mainly sPE samples (Figure 4B).
evidence: Directly stated result from hierarchical clustering with reference to Figure 4B

claim: In the validation set, PCA based on the DD gene signature effectively segregated samples in two homogeneous groups.
source: To validate the DD gene signature in an independent cohort of samples (sPE [n = 7] vs. control [n = 4]), PCA based on these transcripts effectively segregated samples in two homogeneous groups (Figure 4C), corroborated by hierarchical clustering (Figure 4D).
evidence: Directly stated result from validation analysis with reference to Figure 4C

claim: The DD gene signature successfully grouped 100% of controls and 85.7% of sPE cases in the validation set.
source: These genes successfully grouped 100% of controls and 85.7% of sPE cases supporting DD in sPE.
evidence: Directly stated result from validation analysis

claim: Of the 120 genes in the DD signature, 94 endometrial enriched genes encode for specific proteins reported by the Human Protein Atlas.
source: Of the 120 genes in the DD signature, 94 endometrial enriched genes encode for specific proteins reported by the Human Protein Atlas (Uhlén et al., 2015).
evidence: Directly stated result from database comparison

claim: 45 of the 94 endometrial enriched genes (47.9%) were included in the transcriptome modulated by ESR1.
source: Interestingly, 45 of those genes (47.9%) were included in the transcriptome modulated by ESR1 (Hewitt et al., 2010), and 43 genes (45.7%) overlapped with the transcriptome and cistrome associated with PGR (Mazur et al., 2015; Figure 5A).
evidence: Directly stated result from comparison with ESR1 transcriptome data

claim: 43 of the 94 endometrial enriched genes (45.7%) overlapped with the transcriptome and cistrome associated with PGR.
source: Interestingly, 45 of those genes (47.9%) were included in the transcriptome modulated by ESR1 (Hewitt et al., 2010), and 43 genes (45.7%) overlapped with the transcriptome and cistrome associated with PGR (Mazur et al., 2015; Figure 5A).
evidence: Directly stated result from comparison with PGR transcriptome data

claim: The DD fingerprint network showed a highly enriched protein–protein interaction in sPE with interconnection between nodes significantly higher than expected (PPI enrichment p<1.0e-16).
source: This DD fingerprint network showed a highly enriched protein–protein interaction (PPI) in sPE; indeed, the interconnection between nodes was significantly higher than the 93 edges expected (PPI enrichment p<1.0e-16).
evidence: Directly stated result from network analysis with statistical significance

claim: Both ER1 and PR were strongly embedded in the network and highly connected with DD fingerprinting.
source: Interestingly, both ER1 and PR were strongly embedded in the network and highly connected with DD fingerprinting, highlighting the interaction of hormonal receptors with notable decidualization mediators such as IHH and MSX2 validated by RT-qPCR (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Directly stated result from network analysis with reference to validation by RT-qPCR

claim: ESR1 gene expression was reduced in sPE patients compared to controls (p<0.05).
source: We found reduced expression of transcripts encoding the hormone receptors ESR1 (p<0.05) and PGR (p<0.001) in sPE patients (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: Directly stated result from RT-qPCR analysis with statistical significance

claim: PGR gene expression was reduced in sPE patients compared to controls (p<0.001).
source: We found reduced expression of transcripts encoding the hormone receptors ESR1 (p<0.05) and PGR (p<0.001) in sPE patients (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: Directly stated result from RT-qPCR analysis with statistical significance

claim: The isoform PGR-B was significantly downregulated in sPE vs. controls (p<0.01).
source: In-depth expression analyses revealed that the isoform PGR-B was significantly downregulated in sPE vs. controls (p<0.01), while the isoform PGR-A was unaffected (p>0.05) (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: Directly stated result from RT-qPCR analysis with statistical significance

claim: The isoform PGR-A was unaffected in sPE vs. controls (p>0.05).
source: In-depth expression analyses revealed that the isoform PGR-B was significantly downregulated in sPE vs. controls (p<0.01), while the isoform PGR-A was unaffected (p>0.05) (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: Directly stated result from RT-qPCR analysis with statistical significance

claim: ER1 and PR-B protein expression was highly expressed through the decidualized endometrium, especially in the secretory glands in controls, but greatly reduced or absent in sPE samples.
source: Both receptors were highly expressed through the decidualized endometrium, especially in the secretory glands in controls. In contrast, their expression was greatly reduced or absent in sPE samples.
evidence: Directly stated result from immunohistochemical analysis with reference to Figure 5I and J

claim: The sFLT1/PlGF ratio has been proposed as a biomarker showing a positive predictive value of 36.7%, with 66.2% sensitivity and 83.1% specificity but its application is effective only 4 weeks before PE symptoms manifest.
source: The sFLT1/PlGF ratio has been proposed as a biomarker showing a positive predictive value of 36.7%, with 66.2% sensitivity and 83.1% specificity but its application is effective only 4 weeks before PE symptoms manifest (Zeisler et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zeisler et al., 2016

claim: There may be a molecular signature associated with impaired endometrial maturation during early pregnancy in women who develop sPE.
source: In this sense, there may be a molecular signature associated with impaired endometrial maturation during early pregnancy in women who develop sPE (Rabaglino et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rabaglino et al., 2015

claim: hESC isolated from patients with previous sPE failed to decidualize in vitro.
source: Our previous work demonstrated that hESC isolated from patients with previous sPE failed to decidualize in vitro, suggesting a role of the maternal factor in the development of this disease (Garrido-Gomez et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Garrido-Gomez et al., 2017

claim: Molecular pathways of dysregulated decidualization in PE are also found in endometrial disorders such as implantation failure, recurrent miscarriage, and endometriosis.
source: In addition, molecular pathways of dysregulated decidualization in PE are also found in endometrial disorders such as implantation failure, recurrent miscarriage, and endometriosis (Rabaglino and Conrad, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rabaglino and Conrad, 2019

claim: The decidua basalis transcriptome at delivery compared with the transcriptome of decidua at ⁓11.5 gestational weeks and in vitro decidualized hESC from women who experienced sPE revealed little, if any, overlap between molecular signatures.
source: The decidua basalis transcriptome at delivery was compared with the transcriptome of decidua at ⁓11.5 gestational weeks and in vitro decidualized hESC from women who experienced sPE. Both analyses revealed little, if any, overlap between molecular signatures.
evidence: Directly stated comparison result

claim: The signature encoding in vitro DD of hESC years after pregnancy overlapped significantly with the dysregulated profile found in decidual samples at the beginning of pregnancy.
source: In contrast, the signature encoding in vitro DD of hESC years after pregnancy overlapped significantly with the dysregulated profile found in decidual samples at the beginning of pregnancy (Rabaglino and Conrad, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rabaglino and Conrad, 2019

claim: Decidual gene expression patterns during the clinically active disease largely differ from those observed during endometrial decidualization at the end of the menstrual cycle and early pregnancy.
source: Thus, decidual gene expression patterns during the clinically active disease largely differ from those observed during endometrial decidualization at the end of the menstrual cycle and early pregnancy, perhaps reflecting a consequence rather than the origin of sPE.
evidence: Stated as inference from comparison results

claim: The sPE-DD signature includes genes that allowed segregation of samples from the training set into sPE and control groups, which were confirmed by the test set.
source: This sPE-DD signature includes genes that allowed us to segregate samples from the training set into sPE and control groups, which were confirmed by the test set.
evidence: Directly stated result from validation analysis

claim: 90.9% of samples from an independent cohort were properly clustered in the dendrogram.
source: One sPE was misclustered in the test set, such that 90.9% of samples from an independent cohort were properly clustered in the dendrogram.
evidence: Directly stated result from validation analysis

claim: Most of the DD fingerprint genes in sPE were related to the downregulation of ESR1 and PGR, specifically PGR-B.
source: Interestingly, most of the DD fingerprint genes in sPE were related to the downregulation of ESR1 and PGR, specifically PGR-B.
evidence: Directly stated result from network and expression analysis

claim: Low expression of PGR-B and ESR1 activates endometrial decidualization by dysregulating progesterone and estrogen action.
source: We hypothesize that low expression of PGR-B and ESR1 activates endometrial decidualization by dysregulating progesterone (P4) and estrogen (E2) action.
evidence: Stated as hypothesis based on findings

claim: P4- and E2-related cellular signaling may be compromised, leading to the development of DD.
source: Consequently, P4- and E2-related cellular signaling may be compromised, leading to the development of DD.
evidence: Stated as inference from hypothesis

claim: Stromal cell differentiation, stromal–epithelial crosstalk, extracellular matrix degradation, immune system response, and endothelial function may all be disrupted by low expression of PGR-B and ESR1.
source: Stromal cell differentiation, stromal–epithelial crosstalk (Wang et al., 2017), extracellular matrix degradation (Itoh et al., 2012), immune system response, and endothelial function (Okada et al., 2018) may all be disrupted by low expression of PGR-B and ESR1.
evidence: Stated as inference with supporting citations

claim: The local immune system appeared to be dysregulated due to the altered expression of interleukins, cytokines, chemokines, and immunoglobulin.
source: Remarkably, the local immune system appeared to be dysregulated due to the altered expression of interleukins, cytokines, chemokines, and immunoglobulin, which could disrupt the tolerant microenvironment at the maternal–fetal interface in pregnancy and contribute to the development of sPE (Erlebacher, 2013; Harris et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated as observation from data with supporting citations

claim: In non-sPE pregnancies balanced hormonal signaling leads to proper decidualization, which in turn interacts with immune and endothelial cells to control cytotrophoblast invasion.
source: Based on our findings, we postulate that in non-sPE pregnancies balanced hormonal signaling leads to proper decidualization, which in turn interacts with immune and endothelial cells to control cytotrophoblast invasion (Figure 6A).
evidence: Stated as postulate based on findings with reference to Figure 6A

claim: P4 and E2 activate their receptors in the epithelium and signal to the stromal compartment.
source: P4 and E2 activate their receptors in the epithelium and signal to the stromal compartment.
evidence: Stated as part of proposed mechanism

claim: Stromal PR is activated by ER1, which induces target genes involved in decidualization such as MSX2, CCNB1, and IL6.
source: Likewise, stromal PR is activated by ER1, which induces target genes involved in decidualization such as MSX2, CCNB1, and IL6.
evidence: Stated as part of proposed mechanism

claim: In sPE, endometrial ESR1 and IHH are downregulated, decreasing PGR expression and leading to compromised decidualization, endothelial dysfunction, and local immune dysregulation.
source: In contrast, in sPE, endometrial ESR1 and IHH are downregulated, decreasing PGR expression (Figure 6B) and leading to compromised decidualization, endothelial dysfunction, and local immune dysregulation.
evidence: Stated as proposed mechanism based on findings with reference to Figure 6B

claim: In sPE, there is evidence of impaired epithelial–stromal crosstalk through IHH and FGF1, which could lead to an imbalance of hESC proliferation and differentiation.
source: In sPE, we found evidence of impaired epithelial–stromal crosstalk through IHH and FGF1, which could lead to an imbalance of hESC proliferation and differentiation (Cha et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated as inference from data with supporting citations

claim: Downregulated genes involved in stromal cell differentiation in sPE include IL6, CCNB1, CCNB2, and MSX2.
source: In support of this, we observed downregulated genes involved in stromal cell differentiation including IL6, CCNB1, CCNB2, and MSX2.
evidence: Directly stated result from data analysis

claim: Metalloproteinases such as MMP1, MMP7, and MMP11 were downregulated in sPE, which could be associated to defective cell motility and extracellular matrix degradation.
source: Further, metalloproteinases such as MMP1, MMP7, and MMP11 were downregulated in sPE, which could be associated to defective cell motility and extracellular matrix degradation.
evidence: Stated as inference from data

claim: EGR3 and MMP3 are connected to endothelial and immune system dysfunction in sPE and are associated with altered angiogenesis.
source: Other transcriptomic deregulations in sPE are connected to endothelial and immune system dysfunction, such as EGR3 and MMP3, both of which are associated with altered angiogenesis (Chen et al., 2020; Frieling et al., 2020); TNF is involved in endothelial inflammation disbalance (Marcos-Ramiro et al., 2014) and influences the tolerant microenvironment at the maternal–fetal interface (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated as inference from data with supporting citations

claim: TNF is involved in endothelial inflammation disbalance and influences the tolerant microenvironment at the maternal–fetal interface.
source: Other transcriptomic deregulations in sPE are connected to endothelial and immune system dysfunction, such as EGR3 and MMP3, both of which are associated with altered angiogenesis (Chen et al., 2020; Frieling et al., 2020); TNF is involved in endothelial inflammation disbalance (Marcos-Ramiro et al., 2014) and influences the tolerant microenvironment at the maternal–fetal interface (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Marcos-Ramiro et al., 2014 and Li et al., 2018

claim: The potential origin of sPE may lie in the downregulation of ESR1 and PGR-B.
source: The potential origin of sPE may lie in the downregulation of ESR1 and PGR-B.

source: E2 and P4 act through ER1 and PR in the epithelium and stroma and modulate the transcriptome and to promote crosstalk between both compartments (Winuthayanon et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Winuthayanon et al., 2010

claim: ER1 in the epithelium regulates stromal decidualization via paracrine mechanisms mediated by leukemia inhibitory factor, which controls IHH expression that transduce the signal activation of PR in the stroma.
source: ER1 in the epithelium regulates stromal decidualization via paracrine mechanisms mediated by leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF), which controls IHH expression that transduce the signal activation of PR in the stroma (Pawar et al., 2015).

claim: Stromal ER1 activates PR in the same compartment.
source: Also, stromal ER1 activates PR in the same compartment (Kaya Okur et al., 2016).

claim: An endometrial transcriptomic signature persists years after the affected pregnancy.
source: Our findings indicate that an endometrial transcriptomic signature persists years after the affected pregnancy.

source: This signature may be leveraged for a preconception or early prenatal screening strategy in assessing sPE risk and may inform the development of sPE therapies.

claim: Transcriptomic profiles were compared by differential expression analysis, revealing no significant changes in the endometrial transcriptome between preterm and term controls (FDR ≥ 0.05).
source: Transcriptomic profiles were compared by differential expression analysis, revealing no significant changes in the endometrial transcriptome between preterm and term controls (FDR ≥ 0.05; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).

source: sFLT1 protein binds to PlGF, preventing its interaction with endothelial receptors and leading to endothelial dysfunction.
